query: Wang Yi China Foreign Minister visit South Korea 2026 postponed Taiwan dispute rescheduled July August 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of my findings on Wang Yi's postponed visit to South Korea:

**Key findings:**

1. **The postponement is confirmed.** Wang Yi's visit — expected in Q1 2026 as a follow-up to the January 2026 Korea-China summit — was postponed. South Korean media linked the delay to a **Taiwan labeling dispute**.

2. **The Taiwan dispute:** On **March 31, 2026**, South Korea removed the "China (Taiwan)" departure/destination fields from its electronic entry card after Taiwan complained about the wording. China objected on **April 14, 2026**, citing its "one China" principle, and local Korean media reported Beijing placed Wang's visit "on hold."

3. **Rescheduling status (July/August 2026):** As of the latest reporting (**July 14 and July 16, 2026**), the visit had **NOT been formally rescheduled with a confirmed date**. A July 14 Korea Times report indicated both sides were discussing a possible trip "as early as next month" (i.e., **August 2026**), but no firm date was confirmed. A July 16 report said the visit had only reached "the stage of trying to coordinate a possible time."

4. **Additional factors:** China's reluctance was also attributed to South Korea strengthening cooperation with the US, Japan, and NATO. Notably, Wang instead visited North Korea in April 2026, underscoring the contrast between stalled China-South Korea and active China-North Korea exchanges.

**Important caveat:** No source confirmed a finalized August 2026 date — it was a possibility under discussion, not a confirmed rescheduled visit. Also, the AskNews newswire tools were unavailable (inactive subscription), so findings rely on web search and article fetches.

key_facts: Wang Yi's visit to South Korea was expected in Q1 2026 as a follow-up to the January 2026 Korea-China summit, but was postponed.

The postponement was linked by South Korean media to a Taiwan labeling dispute: on March 31, 2026 Seoul removed the 'China (Taiwan)' departure/destination fields from its electronic entry card after Taiwan complained.
On April 14, 2026, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson objected, stating Taiwan is part of China and that labeling it 'China (Taiwan)' is 'entirely natural,' citing the one-China principle.

As of April 20, 2026, Seoul's Foreign Ministry said no arrangements were finalized; local media reported China had put Wang's visit on hold and discussions had not reached the stage of setting specific dates.
As of July 14, 2026, Korea and China were in close consultations over a possible Wang visit 'as early as next month' (August 2026), but no firm date was confirmed.
As of July 16, 2026, a South Korean Foreign Ministry official said the visit had reached 'the stage of trying to coordinate a possible time'; relations described as 'mired in uncertainty.'
Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said in January 2026 he sought a one-on-one meeting with Wang in the first quarter, which never materialized.
Wang Yi last visited South Korea in November 2023 for a trilateral Korea-China-Japan foreign ministers' meeting.
Additional cited factors for China's reluctance: South Korea strengthening cooperation with the US, Japan, and NATO.
In April 2026, Wang Yi visited North Korea (Pyongyang) and met Kim Jong Un, contrasting with stalled China-South Korea high-level exchanges.
As of the latest reporting (mid-July 2026), no source confirmed a finalized/rescheduled date; August 2026 was a possibility under discussion, not confirmed.
